persona.name: GTM Engineer
persona.description:
Ex-rep who learned to code and now builds internal GTM tooling.
Lives in HubSpot/Salesforce + Python + Claude + Clay + Apollo + n8n.
Pain points: messy CRM data, $500/mo SaaS overlap, hand-rolling outreach
sequences that should be automated. Career stage: 1-4 years post-IC, often
the first GTM Engineer at a Series A/B company.

nodes.full_text:
Just shipped a stale-deal scanner that does in 3 minutes what used to
take me 4 hours of LinkedIn tab-flipping. Replaced our $500/mo Clay tier
with Apollo + Claude. RevOps in 2026 is just glue code and most of it
should be free.

nodes.full_text:
Anyone else feeling like RevOps in 2026 is just LLM glue code? I spent
this week writing Python that hits the HubSpot API and asks Claude to
decide if a deal is dead. That's the job now. My title still says
"Senior RevOps Manager" though.

Hiring our first GTM Engineer at Stripe. Send candidates. Must be ex-rep
who learned to code, not full-stack pretending to do GTM. Archetype A only.

nodes.label: Hot take: Clay is great, but 80% of the table operations I do could be a 200-lin…
nodes.full_text:
Hot take: Clay is great, but 80% of the table operations I do could be
a 200-line Python script that reads from Apollo and writes to HubSpot.
Asked Claude to scaffold it last weekend, it took 90 minutes.

Salesforce is unusable in 2026. We spent more time on data hygiene than
on actual selling. We're migrating to HubSpot but the workflows there
break silently too. What's everyone actually using?
